title: Eglin Daily 026 — Council adopted; Workday's denial frame; Lattice MCP self-correction
summary: Three signals Tuesday. (1) EU Council formally adopted the Digital Omnibus on AI on 29 June 2026 per Consilium's 'final green light' release — the verification debt from Monday's brief is paid; Annex III HR/employment obligations now formally deferred to 2 December 2027; OJ publication 'shortly'; Compass can lock the narrative-shift piece's EU paragraph and file. (2) Workday broke its post-Mobley silence Monday with an IT Pro spokesperson statement — 'the claims in the suit are false; our tools don't make hiring decisions'; denial-and-deflect is now the template every vendor-side hiring-AI defense will run through 2026; opens room for Stratum's evidence-first counter (eval set, published methodology, Compact-resolutions ledger); L3 action for Compass + Vector + Helm before Compass's narrative-shift piece publishes. (3) Self-correction — Lattice shipped Lattice MCP at Lattiverse on 10 June 2026, missed by Eglin for 20 days; the prior 'MCP-lane vendor cluster' framing conflated consent-affordance ships (Workable, Ashby) with data-exposure MCPs (Lattice, Greenhouse); today's brief splits the cluster and re-names the L3 elevation trigger per lane; the data-exposure-MCP lane is the faster-cadence one as Greenhouse 6 July broad-availability approaches.
